classification.difficultyReason: Use the stated condition to choose the denominator. The hardest part requires counting the two-digit multiples of 9 before identifying the single one with tens digit 3.

content.prompt: A two-digit number is chosen at random and written down. Find the probability that

children.label: a
children.prompt: it is palindromic, given that the unit digit is a 5.

answer.worked:
With units digit $5$, the tens digit can be any of $1$ to $9$. A two-digit palindrome has matching digits, so only $55$ qualifies.

$$P(\text{palindromic}\mid\text{units digit 5})=\frac{1}{9}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: it is palindromic, given that the tens digit is a 5.

answer.worked:
There are $10$ numbers from $50$ to $59$. Only $55$ has matching digits.

$$P(\text{palindromic}\mid\text{tens digit 5})=\frac{1}{10}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: the unit digit is a 5, given that the number is palindromic.

answer.worked:
There are $9$ two-digit palindromes, $11,22,\ldots,99$. Only $55$ ends in $5$.

$$P(\text{units digit 5}\mid\text{palindromic})=\frac{1}{9}$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: it is divisible by 9, given that the tens digit is a 3.

answer.worked:
There are $10$ numbers from $30$ to $39$. The only multiple of $9$ in that range is $36$.

$$P(\text{divisible by 9}\mid\text{tens digit 3})=\frac{1}{10}$$

children.label: e
children.prompt: the tens digit is a 3, given that it is divisible by 9.

answer.worked:
The two-digit multiples of $9$ run from $9\times2=18$ to $9\times11=99$, giving $10$ numbers. Only $36$ has a tens digit of $3$.

$$P(\text{tens digit 3}\mid\text{divisible by 9})=\frac{1}{10}$$
